summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and prior percutaneous coronary interventions, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, chest pressure on exertion, leg swelling, and recent weight gain. He denied typical anginal pain, and serial EKGs and cardiac enzymes were unchanged and negative, ruling out acute coronary syndrome. Chest imaging showed signs of fluid overload and chronic bronchiectasis. He was diagnosed with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure and treated with intravenous furosemide and the addition of spironolactone. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home in stable condition on optimized medical therapy, including continued antiplatelet, beta-blocker, and statin treatment. He was advised on fluid and salt restriction, daily weight monitoring, and outpatient follow-up with lab testing for electrolyte monitoring.
